transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?
I... I’ve been thinking a lot about whether my family would be better off if I just weren’t here anymore. It's just gotten so hard to keep going, and I don't know what else to do.
Did these feelings start after a specific stressful event or loss, or have they been coming on without any clear trigger? How long have you been feeling this way?

It really started about nine months ago when my husband’s health got much worse and I had to take on almost all of his caregiving. The stress just became too much, and after I crashed from a period where I was running on high energy, this heavy, hopeless feeling took over. It's been like this almost every day since then.

Before this episode started, have you ever had a similar period of depression or low mood that lasted at least two weeks? And has this current low mood been present most days for nearly every day over the past nine months?

No, I’ve never experienced a depression or low period like this before this current cycle started. And yes, this heavy, hopeless feeling has been with me almost every single day for the last nine months, especially after I crashed from that high period.
Have you ever had a similar depressive episode before this one, even if it was less severe or lasted a shorter time?
No, I don't recall ever feeling like this before in my life. This whole cycle of crashing and feeling so incredibly low is completely new to me.

Did these symptoms begin within a few months after a major stressful event or life change, and have they been mainly tied to that stressor? Or have they continued for a long time even after the stressor changed or improved?

Yes, this entire cycle started about nine months ago, right when my husband's health began to decline and I had to take on his caregiving. The stress has been ongoing and hasn't really let up, and my feelings have only persisted and gotten worse over this time.
Have your symptoms been mainly tied to the ongoing caregiving stress, or do they still continue even when you get some relief from that stress?

Even though my sister and church friends have stepped in to help with my husband's appointments and household chores, getting that relief hasn't changed how I feel. The heavy, hopeless feeling and complete lack of energy just continue constantly without letting up at all.
When your caregiving stress is lighter or you get a break, do your mood and energy improve at all, or do the symptoms stay just as severe even then?

No, my mood and energy don't improve at all, even when I get a break. Even with my sister and friends taking over the chores and caregiving, this heavy, hopeless feeling has been constantly hanging over me for the past nine months. It doesn't seem to matter what the daily stress level is; the emptiness just stays exactly the same.
Have you ever had a period of at least several days when you felt unusually energetic or euphoric, needed much less sleep, talked more than usual, or felt more confident or impulsive than normal?

Yes, a few months ago I had a phase lasting several months where I felt exactly like that, bursting with endless energy and barely sleeping. I was talking so fast that people couldn't get a word in, and I took on massive projects like expanding my quilt shop and leading church committees because I felt uniquely capable of doing it all. Eventually, though, I just crashed into this current low.
During that high-energy period, did your symptoms last at least 1 week and cause major problems at work, at home, or lead to hospitalization?

Yes, that high-energy period lasted much longer than a week—it actually went on for several months, and though I wasn't hospitalized, it caused massive problems. My behavior became very erratic, leading to major conflicts at home and church over my spending and wild commitments. It eventually got so bad that I had to completely stop running my quilting business, step down from my church roles, and let all my household responsibilities fall to others.

opening_question.question: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The interview confirms a clear manic episode lasting several months with decreased need for sleep, pressured speech, increased goal-directed activity, grandiosity, excessive commitments/spending, and marked functional impairment, followed by a sustained depressive episode with hopelessness, low energy, and suicidal ideation. This pattern is most consistent with bipolar affective disorder. Adjustment disorder and unipolar depressive disorder are less likely because the elevated mood episode meets full manic criteria and the depressive symptoms occur in the context of bipolar illness.
